knowledge_point.title: Determining the Value of a Constant for Which a Given Linear System Is Consistent or Inconsistent

question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=2 \\ -3x+ky &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & k & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & k & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & k-9 & 8\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=2 \\ (k-9)y &=8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=9,$ then the second equation is $0=8,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=9.$

question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y &=4 \\ -3x+ky &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & k-3 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y &=4 \\ (k-3)y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=3,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$. So, we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x-2y=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=3.$
